sections.title: Food I like

q.prompt: Which word means “food made from flour, often for sandwiches”?
q.reason: “bread” means food made from flour, often for sandwiches.

options.fb: “rice” means small white grains you cook and eat.
“egg” means hens lay them; you can boil or fry them.

q.prompt: Where do Tom and Mia have breakfast?

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 2. In this lesson: Food I like.
Say what food you like and don't like.
Here are some new words. Bread. Food made from flour, often for sandwiches. Rice.
Small white grains you cook and eat. Egg. Hens lay them; you can boil or fry them.
Listen and say them. bread
rice
egg.
And some more words. Banana. A long yellow fruit. Carrot. An orange vegetable. Soup.
Hot food you eat with a spoon. Listen and say them. banana
carrot
soup.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: food made from flour, often for sandwiches?
Now some grammar: like and don't like and likes. Say ‘I like’ and ‘I don't like’.
For he and she, say ‘likes’ and ‘doesn't like’. For example: I like rice.
For example: She doesn't like eggs.
Now listen, and read along. Breakfast at Grandma's. It is Sunday.
Tom and Mia have breakfast at Grandma's house. Tom likes eggs and bread.
Mia doesn't like eggs. Mia likes bananas and milk. Grandma makes rice soup.
Tom and Mia like Grandma's soup best!
Another question. The video will stop. Where do Tom and Mia have breakfast?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like bread, rice, egg.
You practised like and don't like and likes. And you read Breakfast at Grandma's.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

sections.title: At the market

q.prompt: Which word means “a place where people buy and sell food”?
q.reason: “market” means a place where people buy and sell food.

options.fb: “tomato” means a red fruit we eat in salads.
“apples” means round fruit, red or green.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 2. In this lesson: At the market.
Ask for things at a market using ‘some’ and ‘any’.
Here are some new words. Market. A place where people buy and sell food. Apples.
Round fruit, red or green. Tomato. A red fruit we eat in salads. Listen and say them.
market
apples
tomato.
And some more words. Fish. An animal that lives in water; we can eat it. Buy.
Get something with money. Please. A kind word when you ask for something.
Listen and say them. fish
buy
please.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a place where people buy and sell food?
Now some grammar: some and any. Use ‘some’ in sentences.
Use ‘any’ in questions and with ‘not’. For example: I've got some apples.
For example: Have you got any eggs?
Now listen, and read along. At the market. Mum: Good morning!
Have you got any tomatoes? Seller: Yes, I have. They are very red today.
Mum: Can I have six tomatoes, please? Seller: Here you are. Anything else?
Mum: Some apples, please. Have you got any fish?
Seller: Sorry, I haven't got any fish today. Mum: That's ô kê. Thank you!
Another question. The video will stop. What does Mum buy first?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like market, apples, tomato.
You practised some and any. And you read At the market.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
